schedule.upon: notice that the equipment is ready for dispatch

included: Manufacture, delivery to site, installation, commissioning and the final examination by a notified body under the Lifts Directive 2014/33/EU.
Layout drawings for approval, and as-installed wiring diagrams and the operating manual on handover.
Maintenance for the warranty period, with call-out during normal working hours.
Two keys for each key switch supplied.
excluded: VAT and any other tax or duty.
Builder's work of any kind: cutting, patching, grouting, fire-stopping and making good.
Temporary power, lighting, scaffolding and site welfare.
Craneage and hoisting beyond a clear roll-able route from the unloading point to the shaft.
Use of the lift before acceptance; a temporary-use agreement is available on request.
An emergency power supply and its changeover contacts.
Painting and finishes other than those stated.
provided: A plumb, enclosed shaft to the dimensions stated, within 25 mm over its full height, with the fire rating the building requires.
A dry pit with a drain or sump pump, a ladder and lighting.
A lifting beam at the shaft head rated for 3 500 kg, positioned to the layout drawings.
Rail bracket supports at each floor to the layout drawings, and rough openings at each landing until the entrances are set.
A three-phase 400 V fused supply to the control cabinet with a lockable isolator, and a separate lighting and socket circuit.
A telephone line or data connection to the control cabinet for the alarm and, where specified, remote monitoring.
A dry, lockable storage area beside the shaft for the equipment on delivery, and free parking for the installation team.
conditions: Prices are firm for orders placed within the validity period and for delivery within twelve months of order; later delivery is subject to adjustment.
The programme runs from approval of the layout drawings and from a shaft ready for installation; delay by others extends it and re-mobilisation is charged.
Changes after approval of the drawings are made by written variation, priced before the work is done.
The lift complies with EN 81-20 and EN 81-50 as in force at the date of this quotation; a change in the law after that date is a variation.
Title to the equipment passes on payment in full.
The warranty covers defects in materials and workmanship, excludes wear, misuse and work by others, and is conditional on the lift being maintained by us.
Neither party is liable for delay caused by events beyond its reasonable control.
maintenance: The maintenance agreement begins when the warranty period ends and runs for the contract term stated, with the charge reviewed each year against the published index of labour costs.
The charge is based on the usage profile stated; sustained use beyond it is grounds for review.
What the coverage stated excludes is quoted and approved before the work is done.
Where the lift is stated to be maintainable by others, the service tool, its passwords and the wiring diagrams are handed over at acceptance and do not expire.
end_of_life: Where take-back is stated, we dismantle and remove the lift at the end of its service life at the price stated, indexed to the published index of labour costs, and return certificates of recycling.
Where it is not, dismantling and disposal are the owner's, and a declaration of the lift's materials is handed over at acceptance so that whoever does the work knows what the lift contains.

particulars.text: The drive returns braking energy to the building's supply instead of burning it in a resistor, typically 20 to 35 % of drive energy in a mid-rise with heavy traffic. It includes the eco package's LED lighting and deep standby.

Destination control groups up to eight cars; collective control up to four. Both run on the same group controller, so collective control can be upgraded to destination control later without changing the cars.

options.label: Destination control (lobby panels)
options.note: passengers are grouped by floor before they board

particulars.text: A destination panel at every landing of the group: one per two cars at the main lobby, one at each upper landing. Each has a 10.1-inch touch display and an accessible mode with tactile keys and voice guidance to EN 81-70 Annex G, or ADA where that applies.
Up-peak, down-peak, lunchtime and balanced modes, switched by time of day or by measured load. The panel shows the car assigned before the passenger reaches it.

options.label: Automatic rescue device
options.note: the car reaches the nearest floor by itself and opens

particulars.text: A battery unit in the controller brings the car at low speed to the nearest landing in the direction of load and opens the doors, within 60 seconds of the mains failing. The controller tests the batteries every month; they are replaced every four years under maintenance.

options.label: Full battery backup
options.note: the lift keeps running through an outage

particulars.text: An online UPS keeps the lift in normal service for 60 minutes after the mains fail, or two hours where a firefighters lift requires it, then parks the car at the main floor and opens the doors.
In the machine room, or, machine-room-less, in a cabinet beside the shaft at the top landing; it needs about 0.6 m² of floor and ventilation to the building's plant standards.

included: For full battery backup: the UPS and its batteries, their changeover to the lift's supply, and battery replacement during maintenance.

variables.note: Region-split like accessibility: EN 81-72 firefighters lift in Europe, ASME A17.1 Phase I/II emergency operation in North America.

options.label: Phase I/II emergency operation
options.note: the brigade recalls the car and then drives it from inside

particulars.text: Phase I recalls the car to the designated floor on a smoke detector contact at a landing or on the building's fire alarm signal; Phase II lets a firefighter drive it from a key switch in the car.

provided: For fire recall: a smoke detector contact at each landing, or a fire alarm signal, wired to the control cabinet.

options.label: EN 81-72 firefighters lift
options.note: protected lobby, brigade switch, two hours of operation in a fire

particulars.text: A firefighters lift to EN 81-72: a brigade switch at the access level, water protection of the car and pit equipment, a rescue hatch in the car roof, and the car at the furthest floor within 60 seconds. It runs for two hours on a secondary supply.

provided: For the firefighters lift: a fire-protected lobby at each landing, a fire alarm signal wired to the control cabinet, and drainage of the pit for firefighting water.

particulars.text: A 10-inch capacitive touchscreen, with physical buttons kept for alarm, door open and door close. Floor names and messages are edited by the owner in the portal, with the connectivity package, or on site with the service tool.

Floor access control is fitted to every car of the order and configured for every landing it serves. Any floor can be left open to all, by time of day or permanently, from the access control system; the lift keeps no permissions of its own.
Fire recall and firefighters' operation override floor access control: once the car is recalled, every floor is open to the brigade.

options.label: Card reader in the car
options.note: a badge unlocks the floors it is allowed

particulars.text: Certified integrations, tested with the access control vendor and kept current at each release: LenelS2 OnGuard, Genetec Security Center (Synergis), Gallagher Command Centre, Honeywell Pro-Watch, Siemens SiPass integrated, Software House C•CURE 9000 and Nedap AEOS. Another system is integrated through the low-level interface, which any access control panel with OSDP or Wiegand inputs and relay outputs can drive, after a compatibility check at layout approval.

A reader in the car operating panel, supplied by us, reads 125 kHz proximity and 13.56 MHz MIFARE DESFire EV2/EV3 credentials and passes each badge to the building's access control panel over OSDP v2 (secure channel) or Wiegand 26/34-bit. The access control system answers with the floors the badge allows, on one dry contact per locked floor at the controller's interface terminal.

Locks the floor buttons in the car. Landing calls stay open: anyone can call the car, and only an allowed badge can send it to a locked floor. It needs collective control: a destination-controlled car has no floor buttons, and access is checked at the lobby panel instead.

included: For the card reader in the car: a reader in each car operating panel, its wiring through the travelling cable to the controller, the dry-contact interface terminal, and a commissioning test of every locked floor.
excluded: For the card reader in the car: the access control system, its credentials and licences, and the access control contractor's engineering and wiring on its side of the interface terminal.
provided: For the card reader in the car: one dry contact per locked floor from the access control system to the controller's interface terminal, and the floor permission data for each badge group.

options.label: Badge at the lobby panel
options.note: the badge names the floor, so the panel routes the passenger to a car

particulars.text: Certified integrations, tested with the access control vendor and kept current at each release: LenelS2 OnGuard, Genetec Security Center (Synergis), Gallagher Command Centre, Honeywell Pro-Watch, Siemens SiPass integrated, Software House C•CURE 9000 and Nedap AEOS. Another system is integrated through the low-level interface, which any access control panel with OSDP or Wiegand inputs and relay outputs can drive, after a compatibility check at layout approval.

Two levels, chosen at layout approval and priced the same. Low level: the building's own reader is mounted in each destination panel and passes the badge to its access control panel over OSDP v2 (secure channel) or Wiegand 26/34-bit pass-through; the access control system grants or refuses and returns the allowed floors on dry contacts or over OSDP. High level: the group controller takes each badge group's floor permissions and each grant from the access control server over our REST/JSON integration API, or over BACnet/IP where the building management system carries floor security. High level is recommended above six cars or twenty-four access groups, where contact wiring grows unwieldy.

The destination panels at every landing that has one. With destination control the car carries no floor buttons, so the floor a badge allows is enforced at the panel that assigns the car, and there is no separate floor locking in the car. A reader in the car is the card reader in the car, an alternative to this option: a lift has one or the other.

A badge read can place the call by itself, to its holder's home floor; badge groups can be given dedicated cars or priority, and visitor badges a single trip. These are configured at commissioning at no extra charge.
The price is per car of the group, whatever the number of panels or interface level.

included: For floor access at the lobby panel: a reader housing in each destination panel, the integration module in the group controller, its configuration against the customer's floor permission data, and a commissioning test witnessed with the access control contractor.
excluded: For floor access at the lobby panel: the access control system itself, with its readers, credentials, controllers, server and licences and any integration licence its vendor charges, and the access control contractor's engineering and wiring on its side of the interface.
provided: For floor access at the lobby panel: the access control contractor's attendance at commissioning, the floor permission data for each badge group, and the network or contact wiring from the access control system to the lift's interface terminal.

particulars.text: Handover is counted in weeks from order, on layout drawings approved within the four weeks the programme allows; a later approval moves handover by the same number of weeks.

options.label: 10 weeks from order
options.note: a slot bought out of the queue, stock finishes only

particulars.text: The ten weeks hold for stock finishes only: painted steel, laminate or brushed stainless car walls. The slot is held for five working days from the quotation's acceptance.

options.label: Dismantled and removed by us, metals recycled
options.note: the old car, machine and rails leave site sorted, with certificates of recycling

particulars.text: The old car, machine, rails and wiring are sorted on site; a certificate of recycling is issued for each metal stream, and hydraulic oil is removed and disposed of as hazardous waste.

options.label: Removed by the customer's contractor before we start
options.note: the shaft is handed over empty, with no assurance of what is recycled

options.label: Evenings and weekends, with the building in use
options.note: for a building that cannot lose its lift by day

particulars.text: Work between 18:00 and 07:00 on weekdays and through weekends, with the landings made safe and the shaft closed each morning so the building is in use by day.

Uptime is measured per car and per calendar year, excluding outages caused by misuse, vandalism, a power failure or work by others; a shortfall is credited against the next year's maintenance charge, at 5 % of the annual charge per 0.1 % below the figure.

options.label: Remote monitoring and diagnostics
options.note: fewer call-outs: a fault is diagnosed before anyone drives out

particulars.text: A 4G/LTE gateway in the controller sends fault codes, trip counts and door cycles to our service centre, so no building network is needed. Where the machine space has no 4G signal, the gateway connects over the building's Ethernet instead.
Data is hosted in the Netherlands and stays in the EU. The owner reads it in a web portal and exports it as CSV; status points for a building management system are offered over BACnet/IP.

options.label: Examination and lubrication; parts and repairs billed
options.note: the lowest charge, and the least predictable cost

options.label: Planned maintenance and minor parts; major components billed
All parts and labour, major components included
Service tool and parameters kept by us
Service tool, passwords and wiring diagrams handed over, without expiry
options.note: another firm can maintain the lift when this agreement ends

particulars.text: The service tool, its passwords and the controller parameters are handed over at acceptance and do not expire. With the wiring diagrams and the parts list in the operating manual, a competent firm can maintain, adjust and fault-find the lift without us.

footprint.module_scope: Making ≈ EN 15804 A1–A3 with a fabrication multiplier; installation ≈ A4–A5; maintenance ≈ B2–B4 over the service life; energy in use ≈ B6; end of life ≈ C1–C4. Benefits beyond the life cycle (module D) are not counted. All figures are illustrative modelled estimates, not a verified assessment.
